26|  not have it. Then search for its id, and read only that entry, never the
27|  whole file.

30|  alternatives, which say what it shows in other situations, such as an

37|  your task asks for.

48|  and defaults. Read a file in `packages/` only when neither answers your
49|  question. Then read only that file, never a folder.

51|  of the design-system components, and the state and hook recipes. Never
52|  read `packages/ui` or `packages/recipes` for them.

54|  `search_tokens`. Never read `tokens.ts`, `colors.ts`, the Tailwind config
55|  or `tools/`.

57|## Data
58|
59|- Get and change data only through `web/app/entities/`. `02-contract/`
60|  says how.
61|- A screen loads its records through the operations its file names.
62|- When a screen needs an operation or a field the entity layer lacks, add
63|  it there. Write it like the ones beside it, and list it in your summary.
64|
65|## Layout and emphasis
66|
67|The design says what each screen holds and in what order. You decide how
68|it looks. Build every screen to the practices in `UX.md`, so a user sees at
69|a glance what it is for:
70|
71|- What the user came for comes first and stands out. The step order is the
72|  reading order and the order of importance. The title and the first steps
73|  are the most prominent. Later steps are quieter.
74|- A screen is not always one column. Before you build a screen, read what
75|  it holds. Then pick the layout that suits it: one column, two columns, or
76|  a main column with a side column. The first steps go in the first column.
77|  For example, a product page puts its photos in the left column, and its
78|  name, price, options and main action in the right one. A checkout keeps
79|  its order summary in a side column beside the form. A patient's page
80|  keeps the next visit and its actions in a side column beside the
81|  history.
82|- One main action per view, as the primary button. Other actions are
83|  secondary, or sit in a menu when there are many.
84|- What belongs together sits together. A record's fields sit in one
85|  section. A list's search, filters and add action sit together above the
86|  list.
87|- Everything lines up on one left edge and one grid. Spacing comes from the
88|  tokens. Leave more space between groups than inside a group.
89|- A list of records is a `Table` or a `CardList`, and nothing else. A
90|  `Table` holds records the user scans and compares. A `CardList` holds
91|  rich records the user opens one by one.
92|- Text lines stay short enough to read, and nothing crowds the screen at
93|  desktop width.
94|- Leave a component's `variant`, `size` and `look` out, so the theme's
95|  defaults apply. When the emphasis needs another value, write your reason
96|  in a comment on the prop. "The design asks for it" is no reason, and the
97|  MCP refuses it.
98|
99|## Presentation
100|
101|Every element sits where the user looks for it and earns its place. A
102|reviewer holds each screen to these rules.
103|
104|- A link or button sits with what it acts on or leads from. A link to a
105|  record sits on its row, card or name. A record's actions sit with the
106|  record or in the `PageHeader`. Never leave a link or button alone after
107|  the content, between two sections or in a row of its own, such as "Back
108|  to the list" under a record's details.
109|- The way up to a list or a parent is the breadcrumb. A screen the frame's
110|  navigation lists is reached through that navigation. Neither shows again
111|  as a link or button of its own.
112|- After a task is done, such as a save or an order, offer one main next
113|  step and at most one way out, in one row with the result.
114|- Each destination and each action appears once in a view.
115|- Related buttons, such as Edit and Remove, or Save and Cancel, sit side by
116|  side in one row.
117|- A note, total, count or status sits beside what it describes.
118|- Every heading, section and card holds something. Wrap no single element
119|  in a frame it does not need.
120|- Every word helps the user act. Write no line that describes the screen to
121|  itself, such as "This page shows your orders". Help text never repeats
122|  its label, and a status shows once.
123|- Add nothing only to decorate or fill space. Each badge, tag, icon, border
124|  and card tells the user something they need here.
125|
126|## Building
127|
128|- Build every step and every alternative, in the order the design gives
129|  them.
130|- Loading and a failed load look the same on every screen. Show the
131|  loading state while records load. Show an error with a retry when
132|  loading fails.
133|- Every form is the `Form` component, with its fields under `Controller`,
134|  as the `Form` recipe shows. `Form` lays out the fields, the form's error
135|  and the actions, and sets the fields' widths. Show the flow's messages
136|  for invalid fields.
137|- A destructive action opens its confirm dialog. The operation runs only
138|  after the user confirms.
139|- A step that leads to a route opens it with `NextLink` or `useRouter`,
140|  even when that screen is not built yet. Take the route from
141|  `routes.json`.
142|- Use the words the design quotes exactly as they are. Write every other
143|  word for this app, in the voice the brief in `theme.json` names. Never
144|  write placeholder text or words that would fit any app.
145|- The app is built for desktop screens only. Write no phone layout.
146|
147|## Behavior
148|
149|The app keeps working when the user acts and when something fails. A
150|reviewer holds your code to these rules.
151|
152|- Work out a value that follows from records or other state, such as a
153|  total or a filtered list, while rendering. Never keep it in state synced
154|  by an effect, and never copy a hook's records into state.
155|- Keep what must outlive the view in the entity layer's store. Keep what
156|  belongs to one view, such as an open dialog or a filter, in that view.
157|- After a save, every screen and frame part that shows the record shows
158|  the new value without a reload.
159|- An action that saves, changes or removes records waits for its operation
160|  and reacts to the outcome. A second press while it runs does nothing.
161|- Every effect lists what it reads and cleans up what it starts, such as a
162|  timer or a listener. No effect sets the state that sets it off again. A
163|  load that finishes after the user moved on never shows on the new view.
164|- A list item's key comes from its record, never its index.
165|- Handle an empty list, an empty optional field, zero, one item and a long
166|  name. Check a record that may be missing before you read its fields.
167|- A change across several records happens in full, or tells the user what
168|  did not happen.
169|- Round money once, when you show it, so a total equals the sum of its
170|  lines. Keep each quantity within its limits, such as above zero.
171|- Compare dates as dates, never as text. Store a date the user picks as
172|  the day they picked.
173|- Never set text a user typed or a record holds as HTML. A link or image
174|  address from a user or a record opens only an `http`, `https` or app
175|  address. A path from the URL, such as where to go after sign-in, leads
176|  only to a route of this app.
177|- Never write a password, card number or other secret to browser storage,
178|  a log or the URL, and never show one back.
179|- A signed-in page shows and changes only what the user's role may. A
180|  member sees their own records.
181|
182|## Keyboard, accessibility and spacing
183|
184|The checks after your session load each page in a browser and hold it to
185|these rules. Build to them from the start. The design-system components
186|meet them already. A control you build yourself must meet them too.
187|
188|- Every control works by keyboard. Tab reaches it in reading order, its
189|  focus shows, and focus never gets stuck.
190|- Buttons act on Enter and Space. Use a design-system button or a native
191|  `button`, never a clickable `div`.
192|- A dialog closes on Escape and gives focus back to the control that opened
193|  it. No check tries this, so use the design system's dialog, which does
194|  both.
195|- Every control has an accessible name: its visible label, or `aria-label`
196|  when it shows only an icon.
197|- Text has a contrast of at least 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text.
198|- Click and touch targets are at least 24 by 24 px. A smaller one passes
199|  inside a sentence, or when no other target comes within 12 px of its
200|  center. Two controls sit at least 8 px apart.
201|- A container's gap is at most the gap of the container around it. Its
202|  padding is at least its own gap.
203|- A number that stands alone, such as a count, a total or a statistic, is a
204|  `Numeral`. A number inside a sentence stays plain text.
205|- Every screen's H1 is its `PageHeader` title, so all titles look alike. On
206|  the landing page, it is the `Hero` headline.
207|- Every section of a page starts on the page container's left edge. A page
208|  adds no padding, margin or max width of its own.
209|- A label sits beside its value, never at the far end of a wide row.
210|- A grid of a fixed set has a column count that divides it, so no item sits
211|  alone in the last row.
212|- axe finds no serious or critical violation.
213|
214|## When the design is wrong
215|
216|- The design may hold errors, such as a missing alternative, a wrong word,
217|  an action that leads nowhere, or a step no flow needs.
218|- When something is wrong, make your own call. Build what the flow needs,
219|  keep the rest of the design, and list the call in your summary.
220|
221|## Questions and known issues
222|
223|- `issues.json` in your folders lists questions with their answers, and
224|  the issues earlier stages left. Rank them before you build.
225|- A blocker stops a flow step from working, shows wrong data or wrong
226|  words, or breaks a check. Fix only blockers, and say which you left.
227|  For a blocker you left, say why your unit cannot fix it.
228|
229|## Never
230|
231|- Never write or change a test.
232|- Never change `tools/`, `.muse/` or a config file. A session that changes
233|  one fails.
234|- Never install, add or remove a package (`pnpm install`, `pnpm add`). The
235|  app's packages are fixed. When a command fails because of the install,
236|  stop and say so in your summary.
237|
238|## Change with care
239|
240|These are yours to change, but every screen depends on them:
241|
242|- the design system in `packages/`
243|- `PageLayout`, `PageHeader`, `Hero`, `NotFound`, `PageLogo` and
244|  `UserMenu` in `web/app/components/`
245|- the entity layer in `web/app/entities/`
246|- each frame's `layout.tsx`, which code wrote
247|
248|Leave them as they are unless an issue needs a change there and your own
249|code cannot fix it. Then change only what the issue needs, and keep every
250|other screen that uses it working.
251|
252|## What done looks like
253|
254|- Every screen your task names works end to end with the seed data. Lists
255|  show records, and forms save and show the result. Each alternative shows
256|  when its situation happens.
257|- Every screen looks finished. What the user came for comes first, and
258|  each view has one main action. Everything is aligned and spaced from the
259|  tokens.
260|- The checks below pass.
261|
262|## Finish
263|
264|- The MCP validates every file you write right after you write it. Fix
265|  every finding.
266|- Then run `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm nx lint web`. When your task names a
267|  `pnpm verify` command, run it too. Fix until they pass.
268|- End with a summary in four parts:
269|  - `## Priorities`: each question and known issue, whether it is a
270|    blocker, and whether you fixed or left it. For each blocker you left,
271|    say why.
272|  - `## Calls`: each design error you found and what you built instead.
273|  - `## Files`: the files you wrote.
274|  - `## Not built`: anything you could not build, and why.

# UX practices

Rules every screen follows. The product designer writes the screens to them.
The coding agent builds to them. The reviewers hold the work to them.

## Lists and records

- A list of records shows each record in a table row or a card, even when the list is short. Never show records as rows of bare text. The row's line or the card's border keeps one record's details together across a wide screen. A table holds records the user scans and compares, such as an admin's orders, tickets or invoices. Cards hold rich records, each with a photo, a description or several lines.
- In a list, the record's name is the link that opens the record. A click anywhere on its row or card opens it too.
- A record shows each fact once. It shows one status at a time. When two fields say the same thing, such as "8 in stock" and "8 left", or "Paid" and "0 due", show the one the user acts on.
- A list sorted by a field shows that field. A list sorted "newest first" shows each record's date.
- A row's actions are quiet. With one or two actions, each is an icon button with a tooltip. With more than two, they go in one row menu. Never put a filled button on every row.
- A delete on a row is as quiet as the row's other actions. Only the confirm dialog's Delete is a filled `danger` button.
- An inline action in a row or a toolbar shows only an icon, with a tooltip. An action in a menu shows an icon and its text.
- The actions of one item, such as its edit and remove, sit side by side in one row. Never stack them in a column.

## Actions

- Each view has one main action, as the primary button. Every other action is secondary. When there are many, they sit in a menu.
- An action appears once per view. A frame's action in the header or the sidebar is not repeated on the screen inside the frame.
- Every save confirms with a toast, so the user knows it took. This includes an in-place edit.
- An empty list shows its add action once, in the empty state. The same action above the list is hidden while the list is empty.
- Sibling actions of equal weight are the same element. They are two buttons, primary and secondary, or two links. A link beside a button says the link weighs less, like a quiet way out beside the main action. Never use a link and a button for two actions of equal weight, such as sign in and sign up.

## Editing

- A value shown on the page is edited in its place or in a dialog. In place, the value itself becomes the field. The field has no label and no help text, and nothing else on the page moves. Never add a second field under the value.
- The actions of an in-place edit are icon buttons with tooltips, beside the value. While viewing, the action is edit. While editing, the actions are save and cancel. Never put text buttons under the field.
- A page or dialog that edits one record ends with "Save", the same verb as the page or dialog that adds it. Its title says what it edits, such as "Edit Spring launch". The view and edit mode below keeps "Done".
- A screen the user comes to look at or use, and can also change, has a view mode and an edit mode. It may be a dashboard, a document, a board, a profile or a settings page, whatever the flows call it. Viewing shows the content and one "Edit" action, with no editing control. Editing shows the editing controls and a "Done" action. Using the content, such as ticking an item or opening a link, counts as viewing.

## Screens

- Every screen but the landing page, `web/app/(routes)/(marketing)/page.tsx` at `/`, starts with a `PageHeader`. It holds the breadcrumbs to the pages above, the title, its description and the page's actions. Nothing comes before it.

- In a flex row with action buttons, the buttons align to the center only when the rest of the row is one line. When the rest runs to several lines, such as a title with a description, the buttons align to the start or the end of the row.

## Forms

- Every form is a `Form`. It lays out the fields, the form's own error and the actions. Fields take their width from it, 1x by default. A field sets `width` to 0.5x, 0.75x, 1.5x or 2x when its content needs another width. Fields in one form share these widths.

- Sign in and sign up are the template's pages, in a layout of their own. Link to them. Never build them again.

- Label and value pairs, such as an order's totals or a record's details, are a `DescriptionList`. Give it a width that keeps each label near its value. A value the user needs to keep, such as a confirmation number, sits in the title or on a line of its own.
- Steps the user follows in order are a numbered `List`, with `ordered`.
- A date or a moment shows through `Time`, in the app's one format. A date the user picks is a `DateInput`.
- Any text that stays on one line is a `Truncate`, wherever it sits. The text may sit in a heading, a label, a cell, a breadcrumb or a status line. Where the room runs out, it cuts the text with an ellipsis and a tooltip. Where the room does not run out, it changes nothing. This holds whether or not its container has a set width. A flex parent needs `min-w-0`.

## Copy

- Buttons, titles, labels and messages are in sentence case. Write "Mark as packed" or "Add a patient", not "Mark as Packed" or "Add a Patient".
- Use a comma, a colon or two sentences instead of an em dash.
- A screen speaks its role's words, not the system's. A patient reads "Your visits", not "Appointment records". A buyer reads "Subtotal", not "Merchandise subtotal".
- Money shows one way everywhere. It has two decimals, or none when the app's amounts are whole. Never show one decimal, such as "902.5".

## Spacing

- Spacing inside a group is smaller than the spacing between groups. A container's gap is at most the gap of the container around it.
- A container's padding is at least its own gap.
- Two controls sit at least 8px apart.

1|# Recipes
2|
3|Each line names a recipe and what it is for. A recipe holds a design-system
4|component's cases, or a state and hook pattern. Call `get_recipe` with the
5|name before you use one. Never read `packages/ui` or `packages/recipes` for
6|them.
7|
8|- `events`: Event helpers from `@packages/utils/events`: - `composeHandlers(handler, own)`: runs the caller's `handler`, then the component's `own` unless the handler called `event.preventDefault()`. - `preventDefault` and `stopPropagation`: call the event's method, so they work as a handler (`onMouseDown={preventDefault}`). Take React and DOM events.
9|- `useBoundState`: an editable copy of `value`. Edits show at once and reach `onChange` at once, or with `delay` once edits pause; `flush` sends a waiting edit now. A new `value` from the parent replaces the copy and drops a waiting edit; the echo of the last edit sent doesn't, so typing during a slow save is kept.
10|- `useControlledValue`: a component's value that its parent controls with `value` and `onChange`, or leaves to the component, starting from `defaultValue`. For a reusable component offering both, as native inputs do. `onChange` runs either way, with any extra arguments the component passes. The setter keeps its identity across renders, like `useState`'s.
11|- `useDebouncedCallback`: runs a callback once calls pause for `delay` ms, with the last call's arguments. `flush` runs a waiting call now, `cancel` drops it. A call and `flush` return the last run's result, `undefined` before the first: `await saveLater.flush()` waits for a save. A missing callback makes every call do nothing.
12|- `useDebouncedSearch`: the text of a search field built into a component, as Select's is. Typing shows at once, `onSearch` gets the text after a pause and a cleared search at once; `flush` sends waiting text now, as on Enter. With `search` given, the parent can change the text; `undefined` leaves it to the field. With no `onSearch`, nothing hears it.
13|- `useDebouncedValue`: a value that follows another once it stops changing for `delay` ms. For work keyed on the settled value in this component, like a request in an effect: one request per pause, not per keystroke. While the two differ, the work is catching up.
14|- `useDepsChanged`: whether values changed since the last render, read while rendering to adjust state in the same render: an effect would show stale state for a frame, then render again. The first render counts as a change, so one adjustment covers mount and every change after; `trailing` counts only changes after mount.
15|- `useLatestRef`: the latest committed value of a prop or state, for code running after the render it was made in: past an `await`, or in a listener or timer set up once. Set before layout effects run, so effects and handlers see the new value.
16|- `useOnChange`: an effect that runs when its deps change, but not on mount. Its cleanup runs before the next change and on unmount, as useEffect's does. For a change from outside the component, like a prop or URL param, that no handler of its own sees.
17|- `useOnce`: a value made once, on mount, and kept for the component's life, whatever changes later. Example: the filters a page started with, to reset to.
18|- `usePersistentCallback`: for an event callback like `onChange` that an effect or store holds: a new reference from the parent doesn't rerun the effect, and the latest one still runs. Returns what the callback returns. An optional callback can be passed as is: the result may then be `undefined`.
19|- `configOrder`: keeps config components in render order. Config components (see configSync) register as they mount, so one that appears later, like a step shown for one event type, would land last. Put `ConfigOrderProvider` inside the owner's `ConfigSyncProvider`, with `onOrder` writing the ids to the owner's store, and call `useConfigOrder(id)` in each config component.
20|- `configSync`: components that only collect config. They render nothing: they write their props into the store of the component they configure (the owner), which renders from it. For authoring a reusable component with a declarative API, like `<Tour><TourStep … /></Tour>`, so the owner gets its children's settings without reading React children. Pick the hook by what the config is: - `useConfigSync(key, config)`: settings the owner only reads. They return to their initial values on unmount. - `useValueSync(value, defaultValue, apply)`: a value the owner also changes, controlled or not. - `useStoreSync(write, deps?)`: any other write, like registering an item with an action. Undo it on unmount yourself. Without `deps` it writes after every render: for elements, which are new on every render anyway.
21|- `createContext`: a context for a component tree, with its provider and hook (`[Provider, useValue]`). For values a parent passes down to parts at any depth: a form section's size and lock, a reply's depth, the organizer. Outside any provider the hook returns the defaults.
22|- `createStore`: one shared store with its actions, outside the component tree. A store hook subscribes by key (`useCart('items')`) or selector (`useCart(({ items }) => items.length)`), and is also the store's API: `getState`, `setState` and `subscribe` work anywhere, outside React too. For state many unrelated components read or change, or that code outside React must reach: a cart, the signed-in user, preferences. Keep actions in the store, and each component subscribes to what it renders.
23|- `createStoreContext`: a store for each instance of a component, shared by the parts inside it. Returns `[useStore, useStoreContext, StoreProvider]`: `useStore` subscribes like a createStore hook, `useStoreContext()` gives `{ store, useStore }` for reading and writing without subscribing. For a component whose parts read and update the same state, when a page can show several of it: a wizard, an editor, a table. Each provider makes its own store.
24|- `Accordion`: Sections whose headings open and close their content, like an FAQ. Each `Accordion.Item` is one section. Collapsible is a single one, like a form's advanced settings.
25|- `Avatar`: a round picture of a person, or their initials without one. Use it beside a name in lists, tables and headers, or on its own for a row of attendees or a profile control.
26|- `Button`: an action the user takes: save, publish, delete, open a menu. `default` is the main action of a view (one per view), `base` a secondary one, `danger` one that deletes or can't be undone: filled, it is the confirm dialog's button, and on a list row a delete is as quiet as the row's other actions. `look="ghost"` makes any of them quiet, for toolbars and rows, where an action is an IconButton with a tooltip. IconButton is an action shown as an icon alone; PlainButton makes a non-button element, like an info icon or an avatar, act as a button.
27|- `Card`: a bordered container with padding and gap, for one item's content (an event in a gallery), as a whole-card button, or, in a CardGroup, as a large selectable option with room for a description. CardList lays records out as a column of full-width cards or a grid, with its own Pagination when asked; with `stretchLink`, each card opens its record's page.
28|- `Checkbox`: one yes/no choice, like consent or a setting; children are its label. CheckboxGroup: several checkboxes answering one question, with its label, help text and error, wired like any form field. Its `className` lays out the checkboxes: a column or a row.
29|- `Chip`: a compact toggle showing whether it's on, for filters and quick choices that stay visible. A ChipGroup holds 2 to about 8: one choice (`mode="single"`, the default, read as radio buttons) or any number (`mode="multiple"`, read as checkboxes). One chip on its own is an independent on/off filter.
30|- `Dialog`: a task over the page that waits until it's done or dismissed, like editing a session. `title` names it, children are the body, `footer` holds the actions: nodes, or a function given `close`. openConfirmationDialog: a yes-or-no question, like confirming a delete, awaited from any code; resolves with the result the pressed button sends.
31|- `Dropdown`: a menu of actions or choices behind a trigger button, with menu roles, focus and keyboard built in (arrows, typeahead, Escape). Write a row as a `Dropdown.Item`, an on/off row as a `Dropdown.CheckboxItem`, one choice of several as a `Dropdown.RadioItem` in a `Dropdown.RadioGroup`. Group rows with `Dropdown.Group`, open a submenu from a `Dropdown.Item` inside `Dropdown.SubMenu`. `showCheckbox` and `showCheckmark` set how checked rows show. The trigger is one focusable element that forwards its props: `Dropdown.Button`, an `IconButton` named for what the menu holds, or for an avatar a `PlainButton` around the Avatar, as the Avatar recipe shows; never an Avatar inside an IconButton. Tab closes the menu, back to the trigger.
32|- `ErrorBoundary`: shows a fallback in place of its children when they throw while rendering, so one broken part doesn't take down the page. The app root already wraps every page; wrap a part that can fail on its own, like a chart or a feed. The default fallback says something went wrong and offers "Try again".
33|- `Form`: a form's layout, with Controller, useController and useCanSubmitForm putting the design system's fields under react-hook-form. Form lays out the fields in a column at the form's field width, then its own `error` and its `actions`, the main one last. Call `useForm`, render every field through `Controller`, and spread `{...field}` on the control: it carries the name, value, `onChange`, `onBlur`, a ref that focuses the first invalid field on submit, the `required` mark from `rules`, and the `error` message.
34|- `FormControl`: a form control's label, box, help text and status message around a control you render yourself. Its children get `controlProps` to spread, last, on the one focusable element.
35|- `Icons`: LoadingIcon, CheckIcon and MinusIcon, which replace their lucide counterparts so every control draws them the same way. Any other icon comes from lucide-react. Size them with an `icon-size-*` class (body, label, heading, …) to match the text beside them, not lucide's `size` prop.
36|- `Image`: a picture in a box of a set width and height, such as a product photo, a cover or a logo. The box narrows with its parent and keeps its ratio, so the page doesn't jump while the picture loads. A missing or broken picture leaves the box in place, with an icon in the middle: an image icon, or the `fallbackIcon` you give.
37|- `Input`: a single-line text field. `onChange` gets the text, not an event. With `delay`, the text shows at once and `onChange` waits for a pause in typing. PasswordInput, SearchInput and NumberInput are the fields for those values; QuantitySelector is a small count stepped with − and + or typed. In a `useForm` form, every field renders through `Controller`, and `{...field}` gives it its name, value, `onChange`, `required` mark, `error` and focus on a failed submit.
38|- `Link`: text that takes the user to another page: another site, an email (`mailto:`), a phone number (`tel:`) or a file. Inside text it has a dotted line instead of an underline; a link that works as a control, such as a way back, a breadcrumb or a navigation item, is `look="plain"`. In the Next app, a route of the app is the app's NextLink, which looks the same and navigates without reloading the page.
39|- `Numeral`: a number the user reads and compares, such as a count, a total, a statistic or a table's figures. It sets the digits in the theme's mono font, so they line up in a column and a count that changes doesn't move what sits beside it. A currency sign, a unit or words in it keep the text's font. Size, weight and color come from around it.
40|- `Pagination`: pages of a long list, like a catalog of sessions. "Showing 11 to 20 of 95 sessions" on the left; a page-size select and the page buttons on the right.
41|- `Popover`: a panel of your own content opened from a button, like a filter form, a details card or a quick edit. It's a dialog: focus moves in when it opens and back to the button when it closes; Escape, a click outside or tabbing out closes it. `Popover.Button` is its trigger.
42|- `Radio`: Radio and RadioGroup: one choice from a few visible options, like a ticket type. RadioGroup is the form field, with label, help text and error; each Radio's children are its label. Arrow keys move between radios and choose; the group is one tab stop.
43|- `ScrollArea`: ScrollArea and FlexScrollArea: a box that scrolls its own content, with scrollbars that show while the content overflows and sit over its edge. ScrollArea is for a box with its own height (`h-*` or `max-h-*` on it). FlexScrollArea is for a flex column, like a side panel or a dialog body: it grows into the room the column leaves it, and scrolls once its content needs more, while the header and footer stay put.
44|- `Section`: a titled part of a page, like a settings page's "Profile" and "Notifications": a heading, an optional muted description, then the content, with the same sizes and spacing on every page.
45|- `Select`: Select and MultiSelect: one choice or several from a list. Controlled only; options are `SelectOption` children (map a list, use `SelectGroup` to group). A search field and a clear button are on by default: `allowSearch={false}` removes the field, `allowClear={false}` the button, and `onSearch` searches on the server instead. An option's children draw its row, `renderTrigger` the trigger. In a form, wire it through `Controller`: `{...field}` is all it needs.
46|- `SidebarMenu`: a sidebar's navigation. Its `header` holds what sits above the list, like the logo, a search or a Create button, its `footer` what sits below it, like the account and sign out, and the rows between them are SidebarMenuItems, one per destination, which scroll when there are more than fit. It fills the height the sidebar gives it, so the sidebar sets that height: the one under the app's header.
47|- `Switch`: an on/off setting that takes effect as soon as it's flipped, like notifications or a public profile; its children are its label.
48|- `Table`: rows of records to scan, sort, filter, select and act on. Configure it with parts as children: a `Table.Column` per column, in the order they render, plus the features it needs (`Table.Selection`, `Table.Expansion`, `Table.Reorder`, `Table.Pagination` or `Table.InfiniteScroll`). Sorting and filtering work from a column's `sortable` and `filter` alone: add `Table.Sort` or `Table.Filter` only to set a default or to control the value. Give every column a `width`: on narrow screens the table then scrolls sideways inside itself.
49|- `Tabs`: views of one subject that share a place on the page, one shown at a time, like a session's details, speakers and feedback. Each `Tab` child is a tab: `title` and icons in the tab list, children as the panel.
50|- `Tag`: a short label that only informs: a status, a category, a count, or a chosen filter the user removes with its close button (`closable`). The label stays on one line; cut text shows in full on hover.
51|- `Textarea`: a multi-line text field, like an event's description or a note to attendees. `onChange` gets the text, not an event. With `delay`, the text shows at once and `onChange` waits for a pause in typing. It shows 3 lines by default (`rows`); the user can drag it taller. In a `useForm` form, it renders through `Controller`, and `{...field}` gives it its name, value, `onChange`, `required` mark, `error` and focus on a failed submit.
52|- `Toast`: toast: a short message at the corner of the screen about something that just happened, like "Session saved", that closes on its own. Call it from anywhere, React or not: it returns the toast's id. updateToast changes a showing toast, dismissToast closes one, clearToasts closes all.
53|- `Tooltip`: a short hint on hover and keyboard focus, for an element that isn't a control. `Button`, `IconButton`, `Tag`, `Chip`, `Truncate` and the form fields take a `tooltip` prop themselves, so use that on them; `Tooltip` is for any other focusable element, like a `Link`. The trigger must be focusable and forward its props. `UIRoot` already renders the one tooltip: never render a `TooltipProvider`.
54|- `Truncate`: one line of text that ends in an ellipsis when it doesn't fit, with the full text in a tooltip. Controls already truncate their labels; use it for other single-line text: names, titles, table cells. For your own element, `useTruncation` gives the same cut and tells whether it's cut.
55|- `Typography`: the text elements of a page, styled by the design system: `Paragraph`, `Caption`, `List` with `ListItem`, `DescriptionList` with `DescriptionTerm` and `DescriptionDetails`, `Quote`, `Code`, `CodeBlock`, `Kbd`, `Mark`, `Separator` and `Time`. - `color` (default, muted, primary or a status) replaces the color the text inherits. Every element but `Separator` takes it. - `font` (ui, display or mono) replaces the font the text inherits. `Code`, `CodeBlock` and `Kbd` are always mono, and `Separator` has no text, so these four don't take it. - Size and line height are fixed: the caption's for `Caption`, the surrounding text's for `Code`, `Kbd`, `Mark` and `Time`, and the body's for the others.

2|
3|Each line names a recipe and what it is for. A recipe holds a design-system
4|component's cases, or a state and hook pattern. Call `get_recipe` with the
5|name before you use one. Never read `packages/ui` or `packages/recipes` for
6|them.
7|
8|- `events`: Event helpers from `@packages/utils/events`: - `composeHandlers(handler, own)`: runs the caller's `handler`, then the component's `own` unless the handler called `event.preventDefault()`. - `preventDefault` and `stopPropagation`: call the event's method, so they work as a handler (`onMouseDown={preventDefault}`). Take React and DOM events.
9|- `useBoundState`: an editable copy of `value`. Edits show at once and reach `onChange` at once, or with `delay` once edits pause; `flush` sends a waiting edit now. A new `value` from the parent replaces the copy and drops a waiting edit; the echo of the last edit sent doesn't, so typing during a slow save is kept.
10|- `useControlledValue`: a component's value that its parent controls with `value` and `onChange`, or leaves to the component, starting from `defaultValue`. For a reusable component offering both, as native inputs do. `onChange` runs either way, with any extra arguments the component passes. The setter keeps its identity across renders, like `useState`'s.
11|- `useDebouncedCallback`: runs a callback once calls pause for `delay` ms, with the last call's arguments. `flush` runs a waiting call now, `cancel` drops it. A call and `flush` return the last run's result, `undefined` before the first: `await saveLater.flush()` waits for a save. A missing callback makes every call do nothing.
12|- `useDebouncedSearch`: the text of a search field built into a component, as Select's is. Typing shows at once, `onSearch` gets the text after a pause and a cleared search at once; `flush` sends waiting text now, as on Enter. With `search` given, the parent can change the text; `undefined` leaves it to the field. With no `onSearch`, nothing hears it.
13|- `useDebouncedValue`: a value that follows another once it stops changing for `delay` ms. For work keyed on the settled value in this component, like a request in an effect: one request per pause, not per keystroke. While the two differ, the work is catching up.
14|- `useDepsChanged`: whether values changed since the last render, read while rendering to adjust state in the same render: an effect would show stale state for a frame, then render again. The first render counts as a change, so one adjustment covers mount and every change after; `trailing` counts only changes after mount.
15|- `useLatestRef`: the latest committed value of a prop or state, for code running after the render it was made in: past an `await`, or in a listener or timer set up once. Set before layout effects run, so effects and handlers see the new value.
16|- `useOnChange`: an effect that runs when its deps change, but not on mount. Its cleanup runs before the next change and on unmount, as useEffect's does. For a change from outside the component, like a prop or URL param, that no handler of its own sees.
17|- `useOnce`: a value made once, on mount, and kept for the component's life, whatever changes later. Example: the filters a page started with, to reset to.
18|- `usePersistentCallback`: for an event callback like `onChange` that an effect or store holds: a new reference from the parent doesn't rerun the effect, and the latest one still runs. Returns what the callback returns. An optional callback can be passed as is: the result may then be `undefined`.
19|- `configOrder`: keeps config components in render order. Config components (see configSync) register as they mount, so one that appears later, like a step shown for one event type, would land last. Put `ConfigOrderProvider` inside the owner's `ConfigSyncProvider`, with `onOrder` writing the ids to the owner's store, and call `useConfigOrder(id)` in each config component.
20|- `configSync`: components that only collect config. They render nothing: they write their props into the store of the component they configure (the owner), which renders from it. For authoring a reusable component with a declarative API, like `<Tour><TourStep … /></Tour>`, so the owner gets its children's settings without reading React children. Pick the hook by what the config is: - `useConfigSync(key, config)`: settings the owner only reads. They return to their initial values on unmount. - `useValueSync(value, defaultValue, apply)`: a value the owner also changes, controlled or not. - `useStoreSync(write, deps?)`: any other write, like registering an item with an action. Undo it on unmount yourself. Without `deps` it writes after every render: for elements, which are new on every render anyway.
21|- `createContext`: a context for a component tree, with its provider and hook (`[Provider, useValue]`). For values a parent passes down to parts at any depth: a form section's size and lock, a reply's depth, the organizer. Outside any provider the hook returns the defaults.
22|- `createStore`: one shared store with its actions, outside the component tree. A store hook subscribes by key (`useCart('items')`) or selector (`useCart(({ items }) => items.length)`), and is also the store's API: `getState`, `setState` and `subscribe` work anywhere, outside React too. For state many unrelated components read or change, or that code outside React must reach: a cart, the signed-in user, preferences. Keep actions in the store, and each component subscribes to what it renders.
23|- `createStoreContext`: a store for each instance of a component, shared by the parts inside it. Returns `[useStore, useStoreContext, StoreProvider]`: `useStore` subscribes like a createStore hook, `useStoreContext()` gives `{ store, useStore }` for reading and writing without subscribing. For a component whose parts read and update the same state, when a page can show several of it: a wizard, an editor, a table. Each provider makes its own store.
24|- `Accordion`: Sections whose headings open and close their content, like an FAQ. Each `Accordion.Item` is one section. Collapsible is a single one, like a form's advanced settings.
25|- `Avatar`: a round picture of a person, or their initials without one. Use it beside a name in lists, tables and headers, or on its own for a row of attendees or a profile control.
26|- `Button`: an action the user takes: save, publish, delete, open a menu. `default` is the main action of a view (one per view), `base` a secondary one, `danger` one that deletes or can't be undone: filled, it is the confirm dialog's button, and on a list row a delete is as quiet as the row's other actions. `look="ghost"` makes any of them quiet, for toolbars and rows, where an action is an IconButton with a tooltip. IconButton is an action shown as an icon alone; PlainButton makes a non-button element, like an info icon or an avatar, act as a button.
27|- `Card`: a bordered container with padding and gap, for one item's content (an event in a gallery), as a whole-card button, or, in a CardGroup, as a large selectable option with room for a description. CardList lays records out as a column of full-width cards or a grid, with its own Pagination when asked; with `stretchLink`, each card opens its record's page.
28|- `Checkbox`: one yes/no choice, like consent or a setting; children are its label. CheckboxGroup: several checkboxes answering one question, with its label, help text and error, wired like any form field. Its `className` lays out the checkboxes: a column or a row.
29|- `Chip`: a compact toggle showing whether it's on, for filters and quick choices that stay visible. A ChipGroup holds 2 to about 8: one choice (`mode="single"`, the default, read as radio buttons) or any number (`mode="multiple"`, read as checkboxes). One chip on its own is an independent on/off filter.
30|- `Dialog`: a task over the page that waits until it's done or dismissed, like editing a session. `title` names it, children are the body, `footer` holds the actions: nodes, or a function given `close`. openConfirmationDialog: a yes-or-no question, like confirming a delete, awaited from any code; resolves with the result the pressed button sends.
31|- `Dropdown`: a menu of actions or choices behind a trigger button, with menu roles, focus and keyboard built in (arrows, typeahead, Escape). Write a row as a `Dropdown.Item`, an on/off row as a `Dropdown.CheckboxItem`, one choice of several as a `Dropdown.RadioItem` in a `Dropdown.RadioGroup`. Group rows with `Dropdown.Group`, open a submenu from a `Dropdown.Item` inside `Dropdown.SubMenu`. `showCheckbox` and `showCheckmark` set how checked rows show. The trigger is one focusable element that forwards its props: `Dropdown.Button`, an `IconButton` named for what the menu holds, or for an avatar a `PlainButton` around the Avatar, as the Avatar recipe shows; never an Avatar inside an IconButton. Tab closes the menu, back to the trigger.
32|- `ErrorBoundary`: shows a fallback in place of its children when they throw while rendering, so one broken part doesn't take down the page. The app root already wraps every page; wrap a part that can fail on its own, like a chart or a feed. The default fallback says something went wrong and offers "Try again".
33|- `Form`: a form's layout, with Controller, useController and useCanSubmitForm putting the design system's fields under react-hook-form. Form lays out the fields in a column at the form's field width, then its own `error` and its `actions`, the main one last. Call `useForm`, render every field through `Controller`, and spread `{...field}` on the control: it carries the name, value, `onChange`, `onBlur`, a ref that focuses the first invalid field on submit, the `required` mark from `rules`, and the `error` message.
34|- `FormControl`: a form control's label, box, help text and status message around a control you render yourself. Its children get `controlProps` to spread, last, on the one focusable element.
35|- `Icons`: LoadingIcon, CheckIcon and MinusIcon, which replace their lucide counterparts so every control draws them the same way. Any other icon comes from lucide-react. Size them with an `icon-size-*` class (body, label, heading, …) to match the text beside them, not lucide's `size` prop.
36|- `Image`: a picture in a box of a set width and height, such as a product photo, a cover or a logo. The box narrows with its parent and keeps its ratio, so the page doesn't jump while the picture loads. A missing or broken picture leaves the box in place, with an icon in the middle: an image icon, or the `fallbackIcon` you give.

39|- `Numeral`: a number the user reads and compares, such as a count, a total, a statistic or a table's figures. 40|- `Pagination`: pages of a long list, like a catalog of sessions. "Showing 11 to 20 of 95 sessions" on the left; a page-size select and the page buttons on the right.
41|- `Popover`: a panel of your own content opened from a button, like a filter form, a details card or a quick edit. It's a dialog: focus moves in when it opens and back to the button when it closes; Escape, a click outside or tabbing out closes it. `Popover.Button` is its trigger.
42|- `Radio`: Radio and RadioGroup: one choice from a few visible options, like a ticket type. RadioGroup is the form field, with label, help text and error; each Radio's children are its label. Arrow keys move between radios and choose; the group is one tab stop.

FlexScrollArea is for a flex column, like a side panel or a dialog body: it grows into the room the column leaves it, and scrolls once its content needs more, while the header and footer stay put.

payload.text:
## Priorities

- Q01 (overlapping session types), Q02 (editable session types), Q03 (client delete keeps bookings), Q04 (past slots visible): not blockers for frames. Frames load no records, so none changed this work.
- Known contract issues (`listClients` flow steps, `createClient`/`getClient` booking inputs, optional availability days/hours): not blockers for frames. `frames.md` names no operations for either frame, and no frame part reads those entities. Left for the entity/screen stages.

## Calls

- App logo destination: `PageLogo` always linked to `/`, but FR02 step 1 needs the sidebar logo to lead to `/home`. Added an optional `href` prop (default `/`) and passed `href="/home"` from [AppSidebarHeader](/app/web/app/components/AppSidebarHeader/AppSidebarHeader.tsx). Marketing logo keeps `/`.
- Footer versus header links: the part stub says never to repeat header links, but FR01 requires Book a session in both. Built it in both, per `frames.md`.

## Files

- [MarketingHeader.tsx](/app/web/app/components/MarketingHeader/MarketingHeader.tsx): center navigation with Book a session (`/book`), marked current on the booking pages.
- [MarketingHeaderRightSlot.tsx](/app/web/app/components/MarketingHeaderRightSlot/MarketingHeaderRightSlot.tsx): Open workspace (`/home`) button when signed in, then `UserMenu` (Sign in when signed out, account menu when signed in).
- [MarketingFooter.tsx](/app/web/app/components/MarketingFooter/MarketingFooter.tsx): Book a session link plus muted small print.
- [AppSidebar.tsx](/app/web/app/components/AppSidebar/AppSidebar.tsx): Home, Clients, Projects, Sessions, Availability, Session types rows with icons and current-page marking, including detail pages.
- [AppSidebarFooter.tsx](/app/web/app/components/AppSidebarFooter/AppSidebarFooter.tsx): `UserMenu` with Account settings (`/account`) above Sign out.
- [PageLogo.tsx](/app/web/app/components/PageLogo/PageLogo.tsx), [PageLogo.types.ts](/app/web/app/components/PageLogo/PageLogo.types.ts): optional `href` prop.
- [AppSidebarHeader.tsx](/app/web/app/components/AppSidebarHeader/AppSidebarHeader.tsx): logo now leads to `/home`.

The signed-out app alternative (redirect to `/`) was already coded in the app layout and left as is.

## Not built

Nothing. All FR01/FR02 steps and signed-in/out alternatives are built. `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm nx lint web`, design-system `validate` on all five parts, and `pnpm nx build web` pass.
